cards.explanation: The answer is that God's Tent of Meeting was there. Gibeon had the Tent, which Moses, the servant of the LORD, had made in the wilderness. So Solomon, David's son and Israel's king, wasn't just picking a nice hilltop for a field trip. He went where the Tent was, and he took the whole assembly with him.

The answer is Jerusalem. David brought the ark of God from Kiriath-jearim to the place he had prepared for it, because he had pitched a tent for it there. So the ark was in Jerusalem while the Tent of Meeting stood at Gibeon. Two places, friends, and it helps to keep them straight.

The answer is True! The bronze altar made by Bezalel was at Gibeon before the tabernacle of the LORD. The text says Solomon and the assembly inquired of Him there. Bezalel is the son of Uri, the son of Hur, and that altar was right there at Gibeon, friends.

The answer is True. That night God appeared to Solomon and said, “Ask, and I will give it to you!” Think about that for a second, friends. God Himself says ask, and the offer is wide open. Solomon gets to answer however he wants.

The answer is God's promise to David. Solomon says, “Now, O LORD God, let Your promise to my father David be fulfilled.” He's looking back at what God told David and asking for it to come true now that he sits on the throne. The text doesn't spell out which promise he means, so we'll leave it right there.

The answer is wisdom and knowledge. Solomon says, “Now grant me wisdom and knowledge, so that I may lead this people.” Then he asks, “For who is able to govern this great people of Yours?” He's looking at a people as numerous as the dust of the earth, friends, and he asks for what he'll need to lead them.

The answer is long life. God says Solomon had not even requested it, but had asked for wisdom and knowledge to govern His people. Look at the list before it, friends: riches, wealth, honor, even death for his enemies. Solomon skipped all of it, and God noticed every item.

The answer is False. God does grant Solomon wisdom and knowledge, but that's not all He gives. He says, “And I will also give you riches and wealth and honor unlike anything given to the kings before you or after you.” Solomon asked for one thing and God added more on top. That's a full box, friends.
